page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction support for AVX-512 (including VNNI) alongside hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The platform integrates 512 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, and includes 2,577 GB of local SSD storage. It contains no dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded and memory throughput relative to peer instances. The system scores in the top 25% for multi-core compute in stress-ng (62,149.91) and PassMark CPU (61,141.72), as well as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (300.08 GB/sec) and Clang software compilation. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 292.62 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieves 134.23 GB/sec, matching the top quartile. Database operations within PassMark also record top-tier performance at 30,592.05. Conversely, single-core CPU throughput registers in the median 50% across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, demonstrating that parallel scalability is the primary performance driver.

Resource density supports high efficiency for memory-bound workloads by consolidating substantial RAM and high vCPU allocations within a single node, accompanied by bundled local storage for temporary scratch space. A key architectural limitation is the absence of GPU acceleration, which leads to weak throughput for large-parameter deep learning generation tasks, such as 2.72 tokens per second on 70B models. The E64ds_v5 is structurally aligned with production relational database servers, enterprise in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing engines, and large-scale parallel software build clusters.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 260 MB of L3 cache, and 512 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 2,577 GB of local SSD storage and operates without discrete GPUs. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and hardware-accelerated cryptography. Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-threaded processing, PassMark database throughput, and uncached memory bandwidth surpassing 292 GB/sec, contrasted with median single-core metrics. Without specialized accelerators, large language model generation yields low throughput. The instance is suited for enterprise relational databases, extensive in-memory caching, ETL data pipelines, and large software compilation environments.
